The repository tree contains other organizational directories, so folder names alone do not identify the team's maintained seven-category taxonomy or its representative examples. I need that taxonomy before deciding whether this proposal fits.

Review whether the team's maintained seven-category documentation taxonomy already accommodates an INCO Terms proposal. Give the scope and representative entries for each category, then apply its placement logic; do not create the page yet.

The maintained taxonomy is: modes/ for transportation methods such as LTL, FTL, Parcel, Intermodal, Break Bulk, Air, and Ocean; edi/ for X12 sets such as 997, 204, 990, 850, and 810; terms/ for general terminology such as Stops, Route Optimization, Accessorials, Demurrage, and SCAC; parties/ for stakeholders such as Shipper, Carrier, Consignee, Forwarder, Broker, and 3PL; locations/ for Address Formats, Ports, Terminals, and Distribution Centers; packaging/ for Pallets, Containers, Crates, and Drums; and financials/ for FTL Charges, LTL Rates, Accessorial Charges, and Fuel Surcharges. Map HOW freight moves to modes/, X12 transactions to edi/, WHO to parties/, WHERE to locations/, packaging types to packaging/, cost or billing to financials/, and everything else to terms/. INCO Terms are general commercial terminology, so this proposal fits terms/.

Naming uses the .md extension; simple terms use PascalCase without spaces, while compound industry terms preserve spaces and official capitalization. By category: edi/[code].md; modes/[ModeName].md; terms/[Term Name].md; parties/[PartyRole].md; locations/[LocationType].md; packaging/[Unit Name].md; financials/[Cost Type].md. Avoid / \ : * ? " < > |. Each category has README.md, and the root README.md is the entry point.
